$comment: Table of contents for the whole catalog. A pattern is 'animated' when patterns/<slug>/ exists, otherwise 'planned'. Order here is the order everywhere (README, site).

categories.title: Application Architecture
categories.blurb: The big-picture shapes: how a system is split into parts and how those parts talk to each other.

patterns.title: Layered (N-Tier)
patterns.summary: Presentation, business and data layers; each layer only calls the one directly below it.

patterns.title: Modular Monolith
patterns.summary: One deployable unit built from strongly bounded modules that talk through explicit interfaces.

patterns.title: Microservices
patterns.summary: Small, independently deployable services, each owning one business capability and its data.

patterns.title: Event-Driven Architecture
patterns.summary: Producers publish events to a broker; any number of consumers react on their own schedule.

patterns.title: Serverless (Functions)
patterns.summary: Functions start per event, scale out automatically and scale to zero when idle.

patterns.title: Hexagonal (Ports & Adapters)
patterns.summary: Domain logic at the core; UIs, databases and queues plug in through ports and adapters.

patterns.title: Web-Queue-Worker
patterns.summary: A web front end hands slow work to background workers through a queue.

patterns.title: Microkernel (Plug-in)
patterns.summary: A minimal core system extended by independent plug-in modules.

patterns.title: Space-Based
patterns.summary: Processing units share an in-memory data grid, taking the database off the hot path.

patterns.title: Cell-Based Architecture
patterns.summary: Many isolated, identical cells behind a thin router contain the blast radius of any failure.

categories.title: Cloud Infrastructure
categories.blurb: Where workloads run, and how they scale, stay available and recover from disaster.

patterns.title: Multi-Region Active-Active
patterns.summary: Serve users from several regions at once and shift traffic away from a region that fails.

patterns.title: Active-Passive Failover
patterns.summary: A warm standby region is promoted when the primary region goes down.

patterns.title: Disaster Recovery Strategies
patterns.summary: Backup & restore, pilot light, warm standby, active-active: trading cost against RTO and RPO.

patterns.title: Autoscaling
patterns.summary: Add and remove instances automatically as load rises and falls.

patterns.title: Load Balancing
patterns.summary: Spread requests across healthy instances and stop sending to unhealthy ones.

patterns.title: CDN & Edge Caching
patterns.summary: Serve static content from edge locations close to users; only cache misses reach the origin.

patterns.title: Deployment Stamps
patterns.summary: Deploy many independent copies of the whole stack, each serving a subset of tenants.

patterns.title: Hub-and-Spoke Network
patterns.summary: Shared services and egress in a central hub network; workloads live in peered spokes.

patterns.title: Private Endpoints
patterns.summary: Reach managed cloud services over private IPs instead of the public internet.

categories.title: Identity & Access (Auth)
categories.blurb: Authentication and authorization flows: who is calling, and what they are allowed to do.

patterns.title: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE
patterns.summary: The standard sign-in flow for web, mobile and single-page apps: code via the browser, tokens via the back channel.

patterns.title: OpenID Connect (OIDC)
patterns.summary: An ID token on top of OAuth 2.0 tells the app who signed in.

patterns.title: OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials
patterns.summary: Machine-to-machine access tokens, with no user involved.

patterns.title: JWT Validation
patterns.summary: APIs verify token signatures and claims locally, using the issuer's cached public keys (JWKS).

patterns.title: Refresh Token Rotation
patterns.summary: Short-lived access tokens, single-use refresh tokens, and reuse detection that revokes the whole family.

patterns.title: Sessions vs Tokens
patterns.summary: Server-side sessions versus self-contained tokens: where the state lives and how you revoke it.

patterns.title: Token Exchange (On-Behalf-Of)
patterns.summary: Swap an incoming user token for a narrowly scoped one before calling a downstream API.

patterns.title: Device Authorization Grant
patterns.summary: Sign in on a TV or CLI by approving a short code on your phone.

patterns.title: SAML 2.0 Single Sign-On
patterns.summary: Enterprise SSO: the identity provider posts a signed assertion to the app through the browser.

patterns.title: Federated Identity
patterns.summary: Let an external identity provider authenticate users; the application trusts its tokens.

patterns.title: Mutual TLS (mTLS)
patterns.summary: Client and server both present certificates, so every connection is authenticated both ways.

patterns.title: Valet Key
patterns.summary: Give clients a short-lived, narrowly scoped URL to read or write storage directly.

patterns.title: Gatekeeper
patterns.summary: A hardened broker validates and sanitises requests before they reach trusted hosts.

patterns.title: Policy-Based Authorization
patterns.summary: Services ask a central policy engine for allow/deny decisions (RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC).

patterns.title: Zero Trust Access
patterns.summary: No implicit trust from network location: verify identity, device and context on every request.

categories.title: API & Edge
categories.blurb: The front door: how clients reach services, and where cross-cutting concerns live.

patterns.title: API Gateway
patterns.summary: One entry point that authenticates, rate-limits and routes calls to backend services.

patterns.title: Backends for Frontends (BFF)
patterns.summary: A dedicated backend per client type, shaped for exactly what that UI needs.

patterns.title: Gateway Aggregation
patterns.summary: Fan one client request out to several services and merge the answers into one response.

patterns.title: Gateway Offloading
patterns.summary: Move TLS termination, authentication and compression out of every service into the gateway.

patterns.title: Sidecar
patterns.summary: Run helper capabilities (proxy, logging, config) in a separate process next to the app.

patterns.title: Ambassador
patterns.summary: An out-of-process proxy that handles outbound connectivity (retries, TLS, routing) for a client.

patterns.title: Service Mesh
patterns.summary: Sidecar proxies plus a control plane: mTLS, retries and traffic shifting without touching app code.

patterns.title: Webhooks
patterns.summary: Notify subscribers by calling their HTTP endpoints, with signatures, retries and idempotency.

patterns.title: GraphQL Federation
patterns.summary: Subgraphs from many services compose into one graph; a router plans each query across them.

categories.title: Messaging & Integration
categories.blurb: Asynchronous communication, and coordinating work that spans several services.

patterns.title: Publish-Subscribe
patterns.summary: Broadcast each message to every interested subscriber through a topic.

patterns.title: Competing Consumers
patterns.summary: Several workers pull from one queue, so work is shared and throughput scales out.

patterns.title: Queue-Based Load Leveling
patterns.summary: A queue absorbs traffic spikes so the backend can work at a steady pace.

patterns.title: Priority Queue
patterns.summary: Urgent messages are processed ahead of routine ones.

patterns.title: Asynchronous Request-Reply
patterns.summary: Accept now with 202, process in the background, and let the client poll a status URL.

patterns.title: Transactional Outbox
patterns.summary: Save the event in the same database transaction as the data, then relay it: no dual-write gap.

patterns.title: Saga (Orchestration)
patterns.summary: A coordinator runs local transactions in sequence and triggers compensations when one fails.

patterns.title: Saga (Choreography)
patterns.summary: Services react to each other's events to complete a workflow, with no central coordinator.

patterns.title: Dead-Letter Queue
patterns.summary: Park messages that keep failing so they stop blocking the queue and can be inspected.

patterns.title: Idempotent Consumer
patterns.summary: Remember processed message IDs so a redelivered message has no extra effect.

patterns.title: Claim Check
patterns.summary: Put the large payload in storage and send only a reference through the broker.

patterns.title: Pipes and Filters
patterns.summary: Split processing into independent stages connected by channels.

categories.title: Data Management
categories.blurb: Storing, scaling, caching and synchronising data across services.

patterns.title: Cache-Aside
patterns.summary: Read from the cache first; on a miss load from the database and populate the cache.

patterns.title: CQRS
patterns.summary: Separate the write model (commands) from read models (queries), each optimised for its job.

patterns.title: Event Sourcing
patterns.summary: Store every change as an immutable event and rebuild state by replaying them.

patterns.title: Sharding
patterns.summary: Split data horizontally across databases using a shard key.

patterns.title: Read Replicas
patterns.summary: Send writes to the primary and spread reads across asynchronously updated replicas.

patterns.title: Materialized View
patterns.summary: Precompute query-shaped views so reads don't pay for joins and aggregations.

patterns.title: Change Data Capture (CDC)
patterns.summary: Stream every committed change from the database log to other systems.

patterns.title: Database per Service
patterns.summary: Each service owns its data; others go through its API or events, never its tables.

patterns.title: Medallion Architecture
patterns.summary: Bronze, silver, gold: raw data is refined in layers inside a lakehouse.

categories.title: Resilience & Reliability
categories.blurb: Keep serving when dependencies are slow, overloaded or down.

patterns.title: Circuit Breaker
patterns.summary: Stop calling a failing dependency, fail fast with a fallback, and probe until it recovers.

patterns.title: Retry with Backoff & Jitter
patterns.summary: Retry transient failures with growing, randomised delays so clients don't stampede.

patterns.title: Bulkhead
patterns.summary: Give each dependency its own pool of resources so one failure can't sink the whole ship.

patterns.title: Timeout & Fallback
patterns.summary: Bound every remote call and degrade gracefully when the time runs out.

patterns.title: Rate Limiting & Throttling
patterns.summary: Cap how fast each client may call (token bucket) and shed the excess with 429s.

patterns.title: Health Endpoint Monitoring
patterns.summary: Expose liveness and readiness checks that load balancers and monitors probe.

patterns.title: Leader Election
patterns.summary: Instances elect one coordinator; another takes over when its lease expires.

patterns.title: Compensating Transaction
patterns.summary: Undo the completed steps of a multi-step operation that failed part-way.

patterns.title: Chaos Engineering
patterns.summary: Inject failures on purpose to prove the system degrades the way you expect.

categories.title: Deployment & Release
categories.blurb: Ship changes safely, watch them in production, and roll back fast.

patterns.title: Blue-Green Deployment
patterns.summary: Run the new version beside the old one and switch all traffic in one step.

patterns.title: Canary Release
patterns.summary: Route a small slice of traffic to the new version, watch its metrics, then ramp up or roll back.

patterns.title: Rolling Update
patterns.summary: Replace instances batch by batch while the service stays up.

patterns.title: Feature Flags
patterns.summary: Deploy code dark, then turn features on per user or percentage at runtime.

patterns.title: Shadow Traffic
patterns.summary: Mirror live requests to the new version and compare results without affecting users.

patterns.title: GitOps
patterns.summary: Git holds the desired state; an agent continuously reconciles the cluster to match it.

patterns.title: Immutable Infrastructure
patterns.summary: Never patch servers in place: bake a new image and replace them.

patterns.title: External Configuration Store
patterns.summary: Keep configuration out of the deployment package, in a central store read at runtime.

categories.title: Migration & Modernization
categories.blurb: Evolve legacy systems step by step, without a big-bang rewrite.

patterns.title: Strangler Fig
patterns.summary: Put a facade in front of the legacy system and move routes to new services one at a time.

patterns.title: Anti-Corruption Layer
patterns.summary: A translation layer that keeps a legacy model from leaking into the new domain.

patterns.title: Branch by Abstraction
patterns.summary: Introduce an abstraction, build the new implementation behind it, then switch over.

patterns.title: Parallel Run
patterns.summary: Run old and new side by side on the same inputs and compare results before cutting over.

patterns.title: Expand and Contract
patterns.summary: Change a schema or API in backward-compatible steps: expand, migrate, then contract.

patterns.title: Cloud Migration Strategies (7 Rs)
patterns.summary: Rehost, replatform, refactor, repurchase, relocate, retain or retire: pick one per workload.

categories.title: Observability & Operations
categories.blurb: See what the system is doing, and why, when something goes wrong.

patterns.title: Distributed Tracing
patterns.summary: Propagate a trace context across services and assemble the spans into one timeline.

patterns.title: Centralized Logging
patterns.summary: Ship structured logs from every service to one searchable store, correlated by request ID.

patterns.title: SLOs & Error Budgets
patterns.summary: Measure SLIs against an objective and alert on error-budget burn rate, not on every blip.

patterns.title: Telemetry Pipeline (OpenTelemetry)
patterns.summary: Receive, process and export traces, metrics and logs through one vendor-neutral collector.

categories.title: Algorithms & Data Structures
categories.blurb: The must-know fundamentals: how code searches, sorts, recurses and walks graphs, and what each costs as data grows.

patterns.title: Big-O Notation
patterns.summary: How an algorithm's cost grows with its input: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n) and O(n²) side by side as n grows.

patterns.title: Recursion & the Call Stack
patterns.summary: A function calls itself on a smaller input; each call waits on the stack until a base case returns and the answers unwind.

patterns.title: Binary Search
patterns.summary: Halve a sorted range with every check: about 20 steps find one item among a million, where a scan may need a million.

patterns.title: Bubble, Selection & Insertion Sort
patterns.summary: The three simple O(n²) sorts compared, and why insertion sort still runs inside fast library sorts on short runs.

patterns.title: Merge Sort
patterns.summary: Split the list until single items remain, then merge sorted halves back together: O(n log n) every time, and stable.

patterns.title: Quicksort
patterns.summary: Partition around a pivot, smaller values left and larger right, then sort each side: fast in place, O(n²) when pivots are bad.

patterns.title: Binary Heap & Heapsort
patterns.summary: A complete binary tree packed into an array keeps the smallest item on top: O(log n) push and pop, the classic priority queue.

patterns.title: Hash Table
patterns.summary: Hash each key straight to a bucket for O(1) average lookups; colliding keys share a bucket, and the table grows as it fills.

patterns.title: Binary Search Tree
patterns.summary: Smaller keys left, larger right: O(log n) search and insert while the tree stays balanced, O(n) once it degrades into a list.

patterns.title: Two Pointers
patterns.summary: Move two indices through an array, toward each other or one chasing the other, to solve pair and partition problems in one pass.

patterns.title: Sliding Window
patterns.summary: Slide a window along a sequence, adding the item that enters and dropping the one that leaves, instead of re-scanning each window.

patterns.title: Breadth-First Search
patterns.summary: Explore a graph level by level from a queue; the first time BFS reaches a node, it has found a path with the fewest edges.

patterns.title: Depth-First Search
patterns.summary: Follow one path as deep as it goes, then backtrack; a stack or recursion remembers where to resume, and finds cycles too.

patterns.title: Topological Sort
patterns.summary: Order tasks so every dependency comes before what needs it, as build tools and package managers do; a cycle makes it impossible.

patterns.title: Dijkstra's Shortest Path
patterns.summary: Settle the closest unsettled node, relax its edges, repeat: shortest paths from one source when no edge weight is negative.

patterns.title: Greedy Algorithms
patterns.summary: Take the choice that looks best right now and never revisit it: optimal for some problems, quietly wrong for others.

patterns.title: Dynamic Programming
patterns.summary: Solve each overlapping subproblem once and reuse its answer, top-down with memoization or bottom-up with a table.

patterns.title: Backtracking
patterns.summary: Build a solution one choice at a time and undo any choice that hits a dead end: N-Queens, sudoku, permutations.
